title: Anthracite Preferred / AMN / Arlington / Air Liquide / AICI Trust Preferred / Altus / AIFS — Claim Quality V9

notes: Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: AHRPRD 2007, AHRPRD 2008, AHS 2007, AI 2009, AIF-T 2000 and AIF. 2019.
AHRPRD 2007/2008 are Anthracite Series D cumulative preferred shares, not common equity.
AIF-T 2000 is a 9% AICI Capital Trust trust-preferred security, not Acceptance Insurance common.
No source-SQL performance rows exist for these ten ideas.
Anthracite entered Chapter 7 in 2010 after management stated shareholders would receive no value in a reorganization/liquidation scenario.
AMN 2002 is judged using the later VIC author's explicit retrospective that it fell about 40% in under six months.
Arlington 2009 is evaluated using company-reported 2010 book-value growth plus dividends of 55%, avoiding reverse-split chart issues.
Arlington 2012 Short had an accounting-comparability critique but failed to produce the expected >30% downside while book value and dividends remained strong.
Air Liquide return is not reconstructed from raw prices because free-share allocations and the 2016 capital increase complicate comparability; official long-run TSR is used.
Altus' C$36 target was exceeded in 2019; official AIF shows monthly highs up to C$40.29.
AIFS was acquired in 2025 for $2.34/share, but exact 2021 OTC entry IRR is not asserted.

batch_lessons: Preferred seniority does not protect against enterprise-level funding collapse; par value is not a recovery floor.
Static coverage ratios for leveraged finance vehicles must be supplemented with repo-haircut and margin-call stress.
Secular labor shortages and temporary-staffing revenue cycles are distinct variables.
An accounting-comparability critique is insufficient for a Short without cash deterioration and a recognition catalyst.
Post-restructuring financial equity should be valued from economic book and liability structure rather than pre-crisis headline book.
Official total-shareholder-return data are preferable when free-share allocations and rights issues make raw price charts misleading.
Trust preferreds are subordinated credit claims even when they are marketed as income securities.
Vertical software hidden inside service businesses can rerate when recurring revenue and data/workflow moats become visible.
Microcap SaaS strategic value can monetize through M&A, but illiquid historical entry prices should not be invented.
